questions.question: Who was the court poet of king Harshavardhana?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Banabhatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banabhatta** was the renowned **court poet** of **King Harshavardhana**, who ruled northern India during the early 7th century CE.
 
• He is most famous for his classical Sanskrit work, the **"Harshacharita"**, which is a biography of King Harshavardhana.
 
• The **"Harshacharita"** is considered one of the earliest examples of historical writing in Sanskrit literature.
 
• He also authored the celebrated prose romance **"Kadambari"**, which is one of the most celebrated works of classical Sanskrit literature.
 
• **Banabhatta's works** are characterized by their ornate style, deep insight into human emotions, and use of rich, descriptive language.
 
• His writings provide valuable insights into the **social, political, and cultural life** during Harsha’s reign.
 
• King Harshavardhana himself was a patron of art and literature, and Banabhatta's association with him highlights the king's contribution to fostering intellectual and cultural growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vatsbhati**__

 __
 
• **Vatsabhatti** was a famous poet of the Gupta period, who was the court poet of **Kumaragupta I**. He composed the **Mandsaur Prashasti**, which is an important source for understanding the history and culture of the Gupta period.
 
 
 
• **Kalidas**__
 __
 
• **Kalidas** was a classical Sanskrit poet and dramatist, but he belonged to an earlier period, likely during the reign of the **Gupta Empire**.
 
• He is famous for works like **"Abhijnanashakuntalam," "Meghaduta,"** and **"Raghuvamsha."**
 
• Kalidas was not associated with Harshavardhana's court.
 
 
 
• **Ravikriti**__
 
 
• **Ravikriti** was a Jain poet and scholar who flourished during the reign of **King Pulakeshin II** of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• He is known for composing the **"Aihole inscription"**, which narrates the achievements of Pulakeshin II.
 
• Ravikriti was not related to King Harshavardhana.

questions.question: As per Article 181, the ________ can not preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration in the State Legislative Assembly.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Speaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per **Article 181** of the Indian Constitution, the **Speaker** of the State Legislative Assembly cannot preside over the Assembly while a resolution for their removal from office is under consideration.
 
• During such proceedings, the **Deputy Speaker** or any other member of the Assembly, as determined by the rules of procedure, will preside over the session.
 
• The provision ensures **neutrality and fairness** in the proceedings related to the removal of the Speaker.
 
• Article 181 is a specific part of the **Indian Constitution** that deals with the functioning of the presiding officers of the **State Legislature**.
 
• This provision is similar to **Article 96** of the Constitution, which applies to the Lok Sabha Speaker in the Indian Parliament.
 
• The removal process of the Speaker is a significant part of ensuring accountability and is outlined under the **State Legislative Assembly rules.**
 
• The Speaker's role is to maintain the decorum and proper functioning of the Assembly, and such provisions safeguard the legislative process during critical decisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Advocate General**__

 __
 
• The **Advocate General** is the highest legal officer in the State and is appointed under **Article 165** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Advocate General provides legal advice to the State Government and performs duties related to the state's legal matters.
 
• This position is similar to the **Attorney General of India** at the central level.
 
 
 
• **Deputy Chairman**__
 __
 
• The **Deputy Chairman** is a presiding officer of the **Legislative Council** (if the state has a bicameral legislature).
 
• They assist the Chairman in their duties and may preside over the Council in the Chairman's absence.
 
• The Deputy Chairman's role is limited to the Council, and they do not have any jurisdiction over the Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
• **Chairman**__
 
 
• The **Chairman** is the presiding officer of the Legislative Council in states with a bicameral legislature.
 
• The Chairman's role is similar to the Speaker's role in the Legislative Assembly, but their jurisdiction is limited to the Council.
 
• They are elected by the members of the Legislative Council.

questions.question: In 1928, who among the following wrote the Congress Party's Nehru Report, a future constitution for independent India, based on the granting of dominion status?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Motilal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motilal Nehru**, a prominent leader in the Indian freedom struggle, was the father of **Jawaharlal Nehru**, India's first Prime Minister.
 
• In **1928**, Motilal Nehru chaired a committee that drafted the **Nehru Report**, a proposed constitution for India that advocated **dominion status** within the British Empire.
 
• The **Nehru Report** was the first attempt by Indians to draft a constitution, reflecting aspirations for self-rule and independence.
 
• The report rejected the **Simon Commission**, which did not include any Indian representatives, and was a response to widespread dissatisfaction with British policies.
 
• The report proposed measures such as **fundamental rights**, universal adult suffrage, and protection of minority communities.
 
• It emphasized the need for a strong, united India and laid the foundation for future constitutional frameworks.
 
• The recommendations of the Nehru Report, although not implemented immediately, significantly influenced the **Indian independence movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**__

 __
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the son of Motilal Nehru and a prominent leader in the Indian National Congress.
 
• He played a crucial role in the **Indian independence movement** and later became the first **Prime Minister of India** after independence in 1947.
 
• Nehru was known for his vision of a modern, secular, and progressive India.
 
 
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose**__
 __
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose** was an influential leader in the Indian independence struggle and is known for his role in forming the **Indian National Army (INA).**
 
• Bose did not have any direct association with the **Nehru Report** but was critical of the Congress's approach to dominion status, advocating complete independence instead.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**__
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, the father of the nation, was known for his philosophy of **non-violence** and leadership in the Indian freedom movement.
 
• Though Gandhi supported constitutional reforms, he was not directly involved in drafting the **Nehru Report**.
 
• Gandhi's focus during the late 1920s was on mass movements such as the **Salt March** and promoting self-reliance through the **Swadeshi movement**.

questions.question: The Patkai hills are part of the __________ mountains.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Purvanchal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Patkai hills** are part of the **Purvanchal mountain range**, located in the northeastern region of India.
 
• The Purvanchal range includes the **Patkai hills, Naga Hills, Mizo Hills, and Manipur Hills**.
 
• These hills are part of the **Eastern Himalayas** and are characterized by their **rugged terrain** and **dense forests**.
 
• The Patkai hills form a natural boundary between **India and Myanmar**.
 
• The range is known for its **rich biodiversity**, including rare species of flora and fauna.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the climatic conditions of the region, contributing to **heavy rainfall** and a tropical climate.
 
• Several tribes inhabit the region, and the area is known for its unique **cultural heritage** and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Western Ghats**__

 __
 
• The Western Ghats are a **mountain range** located in western India, running parallel to the Arabian Sea.
 
• They are known for their **UNESCO World Heritage Sites** and **rich biodiversity**.
 
• The region is home to several **national parks**, **sanctuaries**, and **reservoirs**.
 
• Major rivers such as **Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri** originate from the Western Ghats.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats**__
 __
 
• The Eastern Ghats are a **discontinuous range of mountains** located along the eastern coast of India.
 
• They are older than the Western Ghats and are characterized by **eroded hills**.
 
• Important rivers like the **Mahanadi, Krishna, and Godavari** cut across the Eastern Ghats.
 
• Major peaks include **Araku Valley** and **Mahendragiri Hills**.
 
 
 
• **Karakoram**__
 
 
• The Karakoram is a **mountain range** spanning Pakistan, India, and China.
 
• It contains some of the world’s **highest peaks**, including **K2**, the second-highest peak in the world.
 
• The **Siachen Glacier**, the world’s second-longest glacier outside the polar regions, is located here.
 
• The region is known for its **extreme climatic conditions** and rugged terrain.

questions.question: In which of the following events did India get its first individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Shooting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India won its first individual Olympic gold medal in **Shooting**.
 
• **Abhinav Bindra** achieved this historic feat at the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• He won the gold medal in the **10m Air Rifle event**.
 
• The victory marked a significant milestone in Indian sports history, making Bindra the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold.
 
• **Abhinav Bindra** demonstrated exceptional skill and mental strength during the competition.
 
• This achievement inspired greater interest in shooting as a sport in India and motivated upcoming athletes to pursue excellence in the field.
 
• The government and sports organizations recognized Bindra's accomplishment, leading to increased support and funding for shooting sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wrestling**__

 __
 
• India has a rich tradition in **wrestling**, and the sport has contributed significantly to India's Olympic success.
 
• Notable wrestlers like **Sushil Kumar** and **Yogeshwar Dutt** have won medals in the Olympics.
 
• Sushil Kumar won a **silver medal** at the 2012 London Olympics and a **bronze medal** at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
 
• However, India’s first individual Olympic gold medal was not in wrestling.
 
 
 
• **Boxing**__
 __
 
• Boxing has gained popularity in India, particularly after **Vijender Singh** secured a **bronze medal** at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
 
• Other notable boxers include **Mary Kom**, who has earned several accolades at international competitions.
 
• Despite these achievements, India’s first individual Olympic gold medal was not in boxing.
 
 
 
• **Weightlifting**__
 
 
• Weightlifting has witnessed significant contributions from athletes like **Karnam Malleswari**, who won a **bronze medal** at the 2000 Sydney Olympics.
 
• While weightlifting has produced commendable performances, it was not the sport in which India won its first individual Olympic gold medal.

questions.question: The term 'foot fault' is associated with which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tennis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"foot fault"** is primarily associated with the game of **tennis**.
 
• A **foot fault** occurs when a player steps on or over the baseline or into the wrong area while serving the ball.
 
• The rules regarding foot faults are outlined in the **International Tennis Federation (ITF) Rules of Tennis**.
 
• This rule ensures that the server does not gain an unfair advantage by stepping closer to the net during the serve.
 
• If a player commits a foot fault, the serve is considered a **fault**, and the player may lose a point if it is a repeated offense.
 
• Foot faults are monitored by the **line umpire**, who is positioned to observe the server's feet.
 
• The term emphasizes the importance of maintaining proper technique and adherence to the rules during a serve in tennis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hockey**__

 __
 
• The term **"foot fault"** is not associated with hockey.
 
• In hockey, players are prohibited from using their feet to stop or control the ball intentionally, but this is not referred to as a "foot fault."
 
• The game of hockey focuses on the use of a **stick** to maneuver the ball and score goals.
 
 
 
• **Archery**__
 __
 
• In archery, there is no term called **"foot fault."**
 
• However, archers must ensure their stance is within the boundaries of the designated shooting line while aiming and shooting.
 
• Archery relies on **precision, focus, and technique** rather than terms like foot faults.
 
 
 
• **Basketball**__
 
 
• The term **"foot fault"** does not apply to basketball.
 
• In basketball, there are specific violations such as **traveling, double dribbling,** and stepping out of bounds.
 
• Players may also commit a **"foot violation"** if they intentionally use their foot to kick the ball, but this is not referred to as a "foot fault."

questions.question:
Calculate the revenue receipts from the following information.

Revenue deficit= 2.80% of GDP Revenue expenditure= 10.80% of GDP
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue deficit** represents the gap between **revenue expenditure** and **revenue receipts**. It indicates whether the government is meeting its day-to-day expenses through its revenue collection or not.
 
• In this case, the **Revenue deficit** is given as **2.80% of GDP**, and the **Revenue expenditure** is provided as **10.80% of GDP**.
 
• The formula to calculate **Revenue receipts** is:
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Deficit**
 
 
 
• By substituting the values:
 
 
• **Revenue Receipts = 10.80% - 2.80%**
 
• **Revenue Receipts = 8.00% of GDP**
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
• **Revenue receipts** are important as they reflect the government’s ability to fund its expenditures and manage fiscal discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Concept: Revenue Deficit**__

 
 
• Revenue deficit occurs when the **government's revenue receipts** are insufficient to cover its **revenue expenditure**.
 
• This is a critical indicator in understanding a government's fiscal health and highlights its reliance on borrowings.
 
• A higher revenue deficit implies lesser funds for **developmental activities** and an increased burden on the economy.

questions.question: When a large amount of carbon dioxide dissolves in a water body, the water becomes acidic because of the formation of which of the following acids?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Carbonic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a large amount of **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** dissolves in water, it reacts chemically to form **carbonic acid (H₂CO₃).**
 
• The reaction involved is: **CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃.**
 
• **Carbonic acid** is a weak acid that dissociates partially into hydrogen ions (H⁺) and bicarbonate ions (HCO₃⁻), which increases the acidity of the water.
 
• The increase in **hydrogen ion concentration** lowers the pH of the water, making it more acidic.
 
• This phenomenon is significant in environmental contexts, such as **ocean acidification**, where the absorption of excess atmospheric CO₂ by oceans leads to increased acidity and affects marine ecosystems.
 
• **Carbonic acid** is not stable in its pure form; it exists only in aqueous solutions.
 
• The process of CO₂ dissolving in water and forming carbonic acid is a reversible reaction, maintaining a dynamic equilibrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carboxylic acid**__

 __
 
• **Carboxylic acids** are organic compounds containing a **-COOH (carboxyl) functional group.**
 
• Examples include **acetic acid (CH₃COOH)** and **formic acid (HCOOH).**
 
• These acids are primarily found in organic chemistry and have diverse applications in **food, industry, and pharmaceuticals.**
 
• They are not related to the dissolution of CO₂ in water.
 
 
 
• **Carbamic acid**__
 __
 
• **Carbamic acid (H₂NCOOH)** is an intermediate compound derived from ammonia and carbon dioxide.
 
• It is used in the production of **urea and other nitrogen-based fertilizers.**
 
• Carbamic acid is unstable and does not exist in significant quantities in dissolved CO₂-water reactions.
 
 
 
• **Carbolic acid**__
 
 
• **Carbolic acid** is an older term for **phenol (C₆H₅OH)**, an aromatic compound.
 
• Phenol is used in **antiseptics, disinfectants, and the production of resins and plastics.**
 
• It has no connection to the chemical processes involving CO₂ and water.

questions.question: Which of the following institutes/projects is declared as a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage of humanity by UNESCO in May 2001?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**National Project to support Kuttiyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuttiyattam** is one of the oldest surviving theatrical traditions of India, originating in the state of **Kerala**.
 
• It combines Sanskrit theatre with elements of traditional Kerala performance art.
 
• In May 2001, UNESCO declared Kuttiyattam as a **masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage of humanity**, recognizing its unique contribution to global culture.
 
• The **National Project to support Kuttiyattam** was initiated to preserve and promote this ancient art form.
 
• Kuttiyattam uses elaborate costumes, intricate facial expressions, and detailed hand gestures (known as **Mudras**) to convey stories and emotions.
 
• Traditionally performed in **temples**, Kuttiyattam is deeply rooted in Kerala's cultural and religious history.
 
• The performances are often lengthy, spanning several days, showcasing the depth and complexity of this art form.
 
• The **Kerala Kalamandalam** is a notable institution involved in the training and preservation of Kuttiyattam artists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy**__

 __
 
• The **Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy** is located in **Imphal, Manipur**.
 
• It focuses on promoting and preserving the traditional dance forms of Manipur, including the famous **Manipuri dance**.
 
• Manipuri dance is known for its **graceful movements, colorful costumes**, and themes derived from **Vaishnavism**.
 
 
 
• **National Institute of Kathak Dance**__
 __
 
• The National Institute of Kathak Dance, also known as **Kathak Kendra**, is located in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is dedicated to promoting and teaching **Kathak**, one of the eight classical dance forms of India.
 
• Kathak emphasizes **rhythmic footwork, spins, and storytelling** through gestures and facial expressions.
 
 
 
• **Music Academy Madras**__
 
 
• The **Music Academy Madras** is located in **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It is one of the oldest institutions dedicated to the promotion of **Carnatic music**.
 
• The academy organizes the prestigious **Annual Music Conference** during the Margazhi season (December-January).

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT pair of molecule/formula units and their molar mass from the following.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**HNO3 - 62**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The molar mass of a compound is calculated by summing up the **atomic masses of all the atoms** in its molecular formula.
 
• For **HNO3 (Nitric Acid)**, the atomic masses of its elements are:
 
 
• **H (Hydrogen):** 1.008
 
• **N (Nitrogen):** 14.007
 
• **O (Oxygen):** 15.999 (per atom, and there are 3 atoms of oxygen).
 
 
 
• Thus, the molar mass of HNO3 = (1.008) + (14.007) + (3 × 15.999) = **63.012 g/mol**.
 
• The given value of **62 g/mol** is incorrect as it does not match the accurate calculated molar mass.
 
• This makes **HNO3 - 62** the incorrect pair in the given options.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CH4 - 16**__

 __
 
• **Methane (CH4)** is a simple hydrocarbon composed of one carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms.
 
• The atomic masses are:
 
 
• **C (Carbon):** 12.011
 
• **H (Hydrogen):** 1.008 (per atom, and there are 4 atoms of hydrogen).
 
 
 
• The molar mass of CH4 = (12.011) + (4 × 1.008) = **16.043 g/mol**, which approximates to **16**.
 
 
 
• **NaCl - 58.5**__
 __
 
• **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** is a common salt composed of one sodium atom and one chlorine atom.
 
• The atomic masses are:
 
 
• **Na (Sodium):** 22.990
 
• **Cl (Chlorine):** 35.453
 
 
 
• The molar mass of NaCl = (22.990) + (35.453) = **58.443 g/mol**, which approximates to **58.5**.
 
 
 
• **HCl - 36.5**__
 
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** consists of one hydrogen atom and one chlorine atom.
 
• The atomic masses are:
 
 
• **H (Hydrogen):** 1.008
 
• **Cl (Chlorine):** 35.453
 
 
 
• The molar mass of HCl = (1.008) + (35.453) = **36.461 g/mol**, which approximates to **36.5**.

questions.question: In animal cells, the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids through β-oxidation is conducted by which of the following organelles?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Peroxisome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Peroxisomes** are small, membrane-bound organelles present in eukaryotic cells.
 
• These organelles are involved in the **breakdown of very long chain fatty acids** through the process of **β-oxidation**.
 
• In animal cells, the shortened fatty acids are further processed in the **mitochondria** to generate energy.
 
• **Peroxisomes** contain enzymes such as **catalase** and **oxidase**, which help in the detoxification of harmful substances, including hydrogen peroxide.
 
• The beta-oxidation in peroxisomes is crucial for the metabolism of specific fatty acids that cannot be processed directly in the mitochondria.
 
• Peroxisomes also play a role in the metabolism of **reactive oxygen species (ROS)** and help maintain cellular health.
 
• These organelles are abundant in tissues like the liver, where detoxification and fatty acid metabolism are highly active.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ribosome**__

 __
 
• **Ribosomes** are responsible for **protein synthesis** in the cell.
 
• They are found in both **prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells** and can be free-floating or attached to the **endoplasmic reticulum**.
 
• Ribosomes do not play any role in fatty acid metabolism or β-oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**__
 __
 
• **Mitochondria** are the **powerhouses of the cell** and are responsible for generating **ATP** through cellular respiration.
 
• They are involved in **β-oxidation of short and medium-chain fatty acids**, but very long chain fatty acids are first processed in the peroxisomes.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**__
 
 
• The **Golgi apparatus** is involved in the **modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids** for secretion or use within the cell.
 
• It does not participate in the breakdown of fatty acids or β-oxidation.

questions.question: How many cities have been selected to be developed as sustainable and responsible destinations as per the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme launched by the Union Ministry of Tourism in January 2023?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**30**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swadesh Darshan 2.0** scheme was launched by the **Union Ministry of Tourism** in **January 2023**.
 
• The scheme focuses on developing **sustainable and responsible tourism destinations** in India.
 
• A total of **30 cities** have been selected under this scheme to be developed as **sustainable and responsible destinations**.
 
• The revamped scheme aims to promote **theme-based tourism circuits** while ensuring environmental and cultural sustainability.
 
• The initiative aligns with the global focus on **sustainable tourism practices** and supports the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• The scheme emphasizes the use of **green technologies**, community participation, and preserving **local heritage and culture**.
 
• It also promotes **employment generation** and enhances the overall tourism experience by providing modern infrastructure and facilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Raga Deepak has been associated with which famous musician?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tansen**__.

__
 
• **Tansen** is one of the most famous musicians in Indian history, known for his exceptional contribution to Hindustani classical music.
 
• He was one of the **Navratnas (Nine Jewels)** in the court of Emperor Akbar during the Mughal era.
 
• Tansen is associated with the **Raga Deepak**, which is known for its legend of creating fire through its rendition.
 
• According to folklore, Tansen's mastery over Raga Deepak was so profound that it could light oil lamps.
 
• He is also credited with creating several new ragas such as **Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Sarang, and Darbari Kanada.**
 
• Tansen was born in **Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh**, and initially trained under Swami Haridas, a renowned musician and saint.
 
• His contributions to Indian music are so significant that an annual **Tansen Music Festival** is held in Gwalior to honor his legacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

questions.question: Balban's rule as an absolute despot led to which of the following events?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Destruction of the Forty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban**, a ruler of the **Slave Dynasty**, was known for his policy of absolute despotism.
 
• Balban believed in the divine right of kingship and sought to centralize his authority by curbing the power of the nobles and feudal lords.
 
• The term **"The Forty"** (or Chahalgani) referred to a group of powerful Turkish nobles who held significant influence during the early years of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Balban considered The Forty as a threat to the central authority of the Sultan and systematically worked to undermine and destroy their power.
 
• He adopted strict policies to suppress rebellion, ensure loyalty, and prevent the rise of factions within the court.
 
• The destruction of The Forty allowed Balban to maintain a strong and centralized administration, ensuring that the Sultan's authority remained unchallenged.
 
• Balban also introduced the concept of **"Zill-e-Ilahi" (Shadow of God)**, emphasizing the Sultan's divine status to reinforce his absolute control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Respected common man**__

 __
 
• While Balban maintained law and order, his policies were primarily aimed at consolidating power rather than focusing on the welfare of the **common man**.
 
• His harsh measures and strict control over the administration left little room for populist policies or direct engagement with the common populace.
 
 
 
• **Granting Jagirs to Nobles**__
 __
 
• Balban was cautious about granting **Jagirs** (land grants) to nobles, as he feared it would strengthen their autonomy and challenge his centralized authority.
 
• Instead, he ensured that the nobility remained dependent on the Sultan for their positions and privileges.
 
 
 
• **Appointed Hindus in administration**__
 
 
• While there were some instances of **Hindus** being appointed in administrative roles during the Delhi Sultanate, Balban's reign was marked by a strong emphasis on centralization and loyalty rather than inclusivity.
 
• His primary focus was on curbing the influence of Turkish nobles and maintaining control over the administration.

questions.question: Which of the following dams is a part of the Damodar Valley Corporation?

__
 
• **Maithon Dam** is one of the dams constructed and managed by the **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC).**
 
• The dam is situated on the **Barakar River**, which is a tributary of the **Damodar River**.
 
• It is located near **Dhanbad in Jharkhand** and serves multiple purposes such as **flood control, irrigation, and power generation.**
 
• The Maithon Dam is known for its **underground power station**, which is one of the first of its kind in Southeast Asia.
 
• The **Damodar Valley Corporation** was established in **1948** to manage and develop the resources of the Damodar River Basin.
 
• The DVC network also includes other dams such as **Tilaiya Dam, Panchet Dam, and Konar Dam.**
 
• These dams collectively aim to mitigate the effects of the Damodar River, which was historically known as the **"Sorrow of Bengal"** due to frequent flooding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is situated in **Uttar Pradesh** and serves as a major source of hydroelectric power and irrigation.
 
• This dam is not part of the **Damodar Valley Corporation** as it lies outside the Damodar River Basin.

• **Koyna Dam** is located on the **Koyna River** in the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• It is primarily used for **hydroelectric power generation** and is one of the largest dams in Maharashtra.
 
• The dam is not connected to the **Damodar Valley Corporation** as it lies in the western part of India.
 
 
 
• **Salal Dam**__
 
 
• The **Salal Dam** is built on the **Chenab River** in the state of **Jammu and Kashmir**.

• This dam is not part of the **Damodar Valley Corporation** as it lies outside the Damodar River Basin.
